title: Halting of the oracle choice machine
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic oracle Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $O$ be a language of Boolean strings, and fix an input $x$ and a configuration $c$ of $N$ on $x$. Let $tape$ assign an optional Boolean symbol to each integer cell, and let $p$ be an integer such that cell $p$ is blank. Then, starting from the configuration obtained by adding this tape with its head at $p$, the oracle choice machine built from $N$ halts after some $s \le 2$ steps. Its output at that time is $c$'s original output if $c$ is already halted, and otherwise is the original output followed by the Boolean symbol $false$.
